IS: 11042 (Part2)-19$r 



Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
BINDING SCREWS FOR ALPINE SKIS 

PART 2 TEST METHODS 



( Reaffirmed 2001 ) 



1. Scope 

2. Tests 



Covers the methods of tests of screws used for fastening ski bindings to alpine skis. 



2,1 Ductility Test — Assembly shall be made in a manner which shall not damage the screw 
threads; at least two complete threads shall overtop the assembly. Drive the test screw into the 
assembly. Using a hammer, strike the edge of the screw head with several lateral blows until a 
deformation of 1 0° shall be obtained. 

2.1.1 Fixation for ductility test — Assembly shall be made in a manner which does not damage 
the screw threads; at least two complete threads shall overtop the assembly. ♦ 

2.1.2 Test assembly — For the purpose of this test, it is necessary to prepare test assemblies, 
representative of material configurations commonly used in ski construction and having dimensions 
similar to those of a cross section of the binding mounting area of an alpin3 ski. 

2.1 .3 Dimensions and material configuration — See Fig. 1 . 




A - Core 20 mm thick, of rigid polyurethane foam, of volumetric mass* Q «■ 0*5 ± 0*05 g/cm 8 , without skin; 

B — Layers 0*8 mm thick, of glass fibre reinforced epoxy laminate finished by sanding ( 60 grit ) on both sides. 
Each layer shall consist of four layers of cloth, each having a mass per unit area of 300 g/m 8 , and shall 
have a glass fibre orientation of 55 percent longitudinally and 45 percent transversely and a glass content 
of approximately 65 percent; 

C — Layers 1*0 mm thick, of aluminium alloy, Ai — Zn 6 Mg Cu, having a minimum tensile strength 

of 600 N/ mm 2 . Both sides shall be sandblasted or etched; 
D — Layers 0'5 mm thick, of acrylonitrile-butadiene-styrene ( ABS ) plastics materials. 



FIG, 



AH dimensions in millimetres. 
1 DIMENSIONS AND DESIGN OF TEST ASSEMBLY 



2.1 A Preparation of test assemblies — In order to avoid non-uniform surface zones due to 
density gradient in the hardened polyurethane foam, 20 mm thick core shall be cut from a block 
having a thickness of 30 mm and from which the material is removed symmetrically. 



♦The density of the polyurethane foam shall be measured before bonding.

Each layer of the test assembly ( see Fig. 1 and 2,1.3 ) shall be bonded using suitable fixture 
under the following conditions: 

a) Temperature : 100°C, 

b) Pressure : 500 ± 100 KPa, and 

c) Curing time : 15 min. 

Assemblies shall be cooled under pressure and allowed to age for one month prior to use for 
testing. 

2,1 .5 Forms of test assembly 

2.1.5.1 Test assembly M — The test assembly shall consist of a core and three discrete layers 
B, C and D on each side of the core ( see Fig. 1 ). 

2.1.5.2 Test assembly P — The test assembly shall consist of a core and two discrete layers 
B and D on each side of the core. 

2 1 .6 Procedure — Drive the test screw into an assembly, using a hammer, strike the edge of 
the screw head with several lateral blows until a deformation of 10° is obtained. 

2.2 Determination of Driving Torque 

2.2.1 Dril and test iig — A jig, as shown in Fig. 2, shall be used for drilling the holes and also 
for determining the driving torque and the stripping torque. The jig shall ensure an exact drill hole 
of diameter 4*1 mm, perpendicular to the top surface of the test assembly, and a minimum 
distance of 50 mm between the holes. It shall also ensure that the test screw is set and mounted 
perpendicular to the top surface of the test assembly. 

For each test, a new location of the test jig shall be used. 

The drill jig bushing shall be made from hardened steel and shall be fixed against rotation. 
The distance plate shall be made from steel of hardness HB 30 about 1 35 and shall have a surface 
roughness of 8 mm. The centering pins shall be used to hold the distance plate in place. 

For determination of the driving torque, the distance plate shall have a thickness of 4 mm. 
For determination of the stripping torque, a plate of thickness 6 mm shall be used. 

2.2.2 Using the drill jig, drill a hole of diameter 41 H12 ( +012 mm ) and depth 9 + 0*5 mm 



in test assembly M. The hole shall not be tapped. 

2.2.2.1 Drive the screw into the hole using the test jig and a suitable torque wrench screw 
driver. Read the driving torque after each half rotation. No lubrication shall be used during this 
procedure and the maximum penetration without contact of the screw head and the distance plate 
shall be 7'5 mm. 

2.2.2.2 Record the maximum driving torque, in newton metres, as the largest measured 
value of the torque applied during the driving procedure. 

2.2.2.3 Repeat the test, using at least ten screws. 

2.3 Determination of stripping torque — Using the drill jig, drill a hole of diameter 4*1 H12 
( + 012 mm ) and depth 7 + 0*5 mm in test assembly P. The hole shall not be tapped. 



2.3.1 Use the test jig to mount and tighten the screws. Apply an increasing torque with the 
torque wrench screw driver until a drop in the torque resistance indicates failure of the thread. 

2.3.2 Record the stripping torque, in newton metres, as the maximum value of the moment 
read on the torque wrench screw driver. 

2.3.3 Repeat the test, using at least ten screws. 

2.4 Static Pull- Out Test 

2AA Pull-out apparatus — Two rolls of diameter 30 mm and 250 mm apart, shall be used to 
support the test assembly "ogether with an attachment plate which permits penetration by the test 
screw to a depth of 8 ± 02 mm in the test assembly.

FIG. 2 DRILL AND TEST JIG 



2.4.2 Using the drill jig, drill holes of diameter 4*1 H12 ( +0*12 mm ) and depth 9 + 0*5 mm 



in test assembly P, ensuring that the holes are at least 50 mm apart. 

2 4.3 Use the pull-out apparatus described in 2.4.1 which allows the introduction of the screw 
perpendicular to the surface of the test assembly to a penetration depth of 8 ± 02 mm, and an 
axial load of the screw perpendicular to the surface of the test assembly during the pull-out test. 

Use a maximum tightening torque of 4 (Mm. 

Position the test assembly such that the test screw is equidistant from the support rolls. 

2.4.4 Apply a load at a rate of 20 mm/min until the screw is pulled from the test assembly. 
Record the maximum load required. 

2.4.5 Repeat the test, using at least ten screws. 

2.5 Determination of Breaking Moment — The screw shall be assembled in a tensile testing machine 
with a minimum of 6 P ( P » pitch of the thread ) exposed, and an axial load applied against the 
underhead bearing face until screw failure occurs. The speed of testing as determined with a free 
running cross head shall not exceed 25 mm per minute. The grips of the testing machine shall be 



IS: 11042 (Part2)- 1987 

self aligning to avoid side thrust on the specimen. The tensile strength of the screw shall be the 
maximum load occurring coincident with that prior to screw fracture ( that is, screw breakage into 
two or more parts ). 

2 5.1 The screw shall not fail with the application of a torque less than the torsional strength 
torque specified in Table 1. 

TABLE 1 MECHANICAL AND PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS

EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This standard is in agreement with ISO 6005-1981 'Alpine skis — Ski binding screws — Test 
methods', issued by the International Organization for Standardization ( ISO ). 

The standard has been issued in two parts: 
Part 1 General requirements, and 
Part 2 Test methods. 



Printed at Printograph, New Delhi, India
